reply_text:
㊥ Partly. One complete real example already works end to end, on four of our turns from 1 October. The agent offered two options, you answered "1", and the system recorded your answer as accepting that offer, with the commit in the same turn carrying it out. That is in §3–4 of the notebook. The newer piece, your `🈸:` replies closing an agent's question, has not yet happened in a stored turn. The tests show it working, but only on examples I constructed. The quickest way to get a real one is for you to answer one of my 🈸 questions with "🈸: yes …". Your next turn would then be stored with that link, and I could show the question closing.

㊢ (what is real today)
- **Your turns are read.** 小象 and then 象 read every turn you send. 1,422 of your turns since 30 September are stored with those readings.
- **Agent replies are read.** 大象 reads the marked paragraphs and commits of real replies. The notebook runs it on the 1 October turns.
- **Open questions are tracked.** Across those four turns, the kernel reports after each turn which offers and questions closed and which are still open.
- **The design-pattern model has been run on one real event.** It used the line in the log written when you switched 象 off on 3 October.

㊩ (what is not yet shown on real data)
- **No stored turn of yours has closed a question through a pointer.** The server began storing pointers at 02:32 this morning. Since then, the only pointer stored in this session (turn 28, "㊟: So it should go into futon1b") answers a caveat of mine, ㊟, which leaves no question open.
- **The reminder machine.** It has been live since this morning, but I haven't checked whether it has nudged anyone yet. If it has, that would be another real example.
- **The bracketed labels agents write after each mark.** My count today showed they can't be linked without a model. So the proforma now asks agents to quote your words in the bracket. That only began today, so there is nothing to show yet.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I check the reminder machine's log for real nudges, and add a §4 example to the notebook as soon as a stored turn of yours closes a question through its pointer?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (informal requisition) Understood. §9 says "requisitioned" there means putting the job where the War Machine will pick it up: either as a mission with an acceptance checklist, or as the target of a controlled click. It also notes that futon2's `**Requisition:**` line means the opposite, so the two senses don't get mixed up in later work.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what §9 contains) The commit is futon3c `8094ecd3`.
- **The job:** one acceptance item, checked by something neither arm controls.
- **The two arms:** they start from the same commit in separate worktrees, and neither can see the other's commits until both are done. Arm W is the War Machine; arm O is an orchestrator such as claude-4 running its own dispatches.
- **What gets compared:** results per acceptance item closed, with every number stating which population it counts. Your turns per closed item is a main measure.
- **The evaluation packet:** the same for both arms. A unit one arm doesn't produce, such as the Morning Brief, is recorded as absent rather than counted as a failure.
- **How many runs:** three or four similar jobs, alternating which arm goes first.
- **What would make it misleading:**
  - the arms getting different specification texts;
  - your interventions counted from memory rather than from the turn records;
  - choosing a job after knowing which arm it suits.
